solutions.check: 27 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: see 22ac.
Members at their thickest, linking Trump's inauguration with really good times

indicators.note: an inauguration is a beginning in office, so only the opening letter of the name is wanted

blocks.note: the first letter of the president's name
highs are peak moments of elation

explanation.surface: A jibe that Trump's swearing-in ushered in a golden era, framed around stout limbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inauguration' reads as a political ceremony, but it only asks for the start of Trump. The legs are 'members', and their thickest part is the upper leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbs are called members, and the upper part of the leg, above the knee, is where each leg is widest.

clue.text: Return to original state, taking drug in break

indicators.note: a thing placed in something sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a rest is a break from work
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone recovering on holiday, popping a pill on their break to get back to normal.
explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy is a standard crossword drug; it goes inside the break.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore a device or system to its starting configuration is the usual computing sense of the verb.

clue.text: What battle-axes do to nipples, sadly

indicators.note: something that has gone sadly has gone wrong, so these letters end up in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wince-inducing picture of what fearsome, domineering women do to men's chests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battle-axes' suggests formidable women, but here it is the weapons; 'to' belongs to the anagram fodder rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An axe used in battle cleaves things, cutting them apart so they gape: the phrasal verb describes that effect.

clue.text: Historic city Trump "started" – "none better"

indicators.note: what something started with is its opening, so only the initial letter of the name counts

blocks.note: Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt and also of ancient Greece
the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A dig at Trump's boastful claim to have founded something ancient that he calls unbeatable.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks mimic Trump's bragging and carry no wordplay; 'started' only asks for his initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying nothing surpasses something is the same as calling it superlative, the top of its kind.

clue.text: see 10ac.
Pissed female getting on Eye cover

blocks.note: British slang: blind drunk, so blind means drunk
F is the standard abbreviation for female
someone getting on is ageing

explanation.surface: A drunk older woman is apparently on the cover of Private Eye magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' is British slang for drunk, not angry, and 'blind' is a synonym. 'Eye' is capitalised to suggest the magazine; the capital carries no wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of cloth tied over somebody's sight is literally a covering for the eyes.

clue.text: Very turned on by Ray's cooked sole

indicators.note: cooked figures have been tampered with, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: so means very, as in so good
a light that is turned on is lit
taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A diner aroused by the fish dish Ray has prepared; sole and ray are both fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray and sole both look like fish on a menu; ray is anagram fodder and sole is the definition. 'Ray's cooked' means Ray is cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole as an adjective means only or single, and a single, lone thing is one of a kind.

clue.text: Theresa May disheartened and pissed with core minister

indicators.note: to dishearten is literally to take the heart out, so the middle letter goes
drunk and reeling, so the combined letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the three-letter month with its central A removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Theresa May, dejected and drunk, alongside a senior government figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'May' loses its heart, not the whole name. Theresa May held this office before becoming prime minister, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The British cabinet member responsible for policing, immigration and domestic security holds this title, so it is a government minister.

clue.text: Hollywood lets in rotten borough?

indicators.note: something rotten has decayed out of its proper form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
a borough is a town with its own corporation

explanation.surface: Hollywood admits a rotten borough, a parliamentary seat with almost no voters, suggesting corruption in the film world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten borough' looks like a single historical phrase but splits: 'rotten' is the anagram signal and 'borough' gives the town.
explanation.definitionFit: A mocking nickname for the film capital, mixing glitter and showiness with the idea of a place.

clue.text: (& 5dn.) A feature of unemployment: Danish-led fiasco

indicators.note: a fiasco is a mess, so these letters end up jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A botched venture headed by Danes leaves people out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Danish-led' looks like a description of the fiasco, but its letters are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers without jobs have nothing to occupy their fingers; the proverb says the devil finds work for them.

clue.text: Pure truss that's brought out on formal occasions

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase rather than a noun: read it with the preceding 'that's' as 'what's brought out on formal occasions'

blocks.note: white is the colour of purity
to truss is to tie up

explanation.surface: A pristine surgical truss, apparently only worn for grand events.
explanation.walkthrough: A truss here is a verb, to bind, rather than the medical support garment the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The most formal evening dress code, with tailcoat and bow, is worn only at the grandest events such as state banquets.

clue.text: Balls wedged in gorge – relax!

indicators.note: something wedged in is jammed inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to gorge is to eat one's fill, to satisfy fully
Ed Balls is a former Labour politician and TV personality

explanation.surface: Something painfully stuck in a ravine, with an incongruous order to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' is not testicles but Ed Balls, the British Labour politician, so it gives his first name. 'Gorge' is a verb, not a canyon.
explanation.definitionFit: To calm a person with a soothing drug is to make them unwind; relax is used transitively in this sense.

clue.text: Trump would like to control this 'liberal' computer user

definitions.text: Trump would like to control this

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so these letters are taken freely and reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Trump wanting to rein in a left-leaning person at a keyboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like a political label for the user, fitting Trump; its quotation marks flag that it means free, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Presidents appoint America's highest judges, and Trump sought a conservative majority on that bench to steer its rulings.

clue.text: Not fully tumescent from house massage one had

blocks.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, one sharing a wall with its neighbour
to massage figures is to rig them
I'd is short for I had

explanation.surface: A disappointing result from a massage at a house of ill repute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Massage' is the dishonest sense, as in massaging statistics. A semi is the British name for a semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: Partly stiff but not wholly so; the prefix meaning half sits on an adjective meaning stiff.

clue.text: Joke's on men cutting tips from reproductive act tackle

indicators.note: a tip is the end of something, so only the last letter of each word is kept
to cut into something is to go inside it, so one chunk sits within the other

blocks.note: a quip is a witty remark
taken as written
the final letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A joke at the expense of men having vasectomies, cutting the reproductive act short.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke and the men go together and are cut into the two end letters. 'Tackle' is also British slang for male genitals, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is gear, the kit needed for a pursuit, as in fishing tackle.

clue.text: Look sexy, grabbing on it, waggling for show

indicators.note: to grab something is to hold it, so one piece holds the other
something waggling moves to and fro, so these letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: pouting the lips is a classic sultry look
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A model posing seductively, grabbing and wiggling something purely for show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For show' looks like the end of the surface sentence, but 'for' is a link word and 'show' is a verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate or draw attention to something is to make it seen, the verb sense of show.

clue.text: Public land pulverized – shared by Donald and Kim?

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase describing the thing, read as 'what is shared by', rather than a noun

blocks.note: a common is open land the public may use
something pulverized has been crushed to powder

explanation.surface: Talk of a flattened public space, then a wry question about Trump and Kim Jong-un's summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un were seeking agreement. A common is a British village green open to all.
explanation.definitionFit: Points of agreement between opposing parties are what negotiators look for, as the two leaders did at their summit.

clue.text: Sexually active? There's danger engaging in extremes of fantasy

indicators.note: a gear engaging in another fits inside it, so one piece goes within the other
extremes are the two far ends, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
a risk is a danger

explanation.surface: A warning that acting out extreme sexual fantasies carries risks.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a playful definition: being amorously playful is not quite the same as being sexually active.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky means playful and lively, and in colloquial use amorous or in the mood for sex.

clue.text: Types welcoming Corbyn's end getting drinks

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: types and sorts are both kinds
the final letter of the Labour leader's name

explanation.surface: People who rejoice at Jeremy Corbyn's downfall celebrate with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corbyn's end' sounds like his political demise but asks only for his last letter. A snort is slang for a quick alcoholic drink, a nip.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a snort is a quick shot of spirits, so the plural noun matches a plural noun for alcoholic tots.

clue.text: Girl from South America – Republican's 'tail'

indicators.note: a tail is the back end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for south
the United States of America
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A South American woman as a Republican politician's 'bit of tail', slang for a sexual partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South America' looks like the continent, but it splits into two pieces. 'Tail' is in quotes for its slang sense; for the wordplay it means the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, and crosswords routinely define any given name by the bare word for a woman or man.

clue.text: Hanging Seal at second attempt

blocks.note: to seal a parcel is to tape it
S is the abbreviation for second
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: An execution by hanging that only succeeded on the second go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' suggests the gallows, but it is a noun: a wall hanging. 'Seal' is a verb, not the animal or the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven textile displayed on a wall is a wall hanging, the classic example being the Bayeux one.

clue.text: Filthy place, son, jug

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: A disgusting room, a boy and a jug: a list describing a squalid household.
explanation.walkthrough: S for son is a standard abbreviation, and a ewer is the old wash-stand jug.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground drain carrying waste water and excrement is about as foul a location as exists.

clue.text: (& 1ac.) Vociferous flier shows strain, having infection

blocks.note: a strain is a melody or tune
a common yeast infection

explanation.surface: A loud passenger on a plane shows signs of stress because of an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' reads as stress but means a tune, and 'flier' is a bird, not an air traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A common European songbird known for its loud, repeated musical phrases, so a noisy bird.

clue.text: US right wing tweeter is sadly familiar with our ways?

indicators.note: the right wing of a word is its right-hand end, its final letter
things gone sadly have gone wrong, so these letters land in the wrong order

blocks.note: the final letter of the abbreviation
taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An American right-wing tweeter, Trump by implication, who regrettably knows how things are done here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right wing' looks political but takes the right-hand letter of US. The question mark flags 'our ways' as the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Being savvy about urban life means knowing the roads and how city people behave, with 'ways' punning on roads.

clue.text: Trainee Casanova on Net, getting floppy

indicators.note: something floppy loses its shape, so these letters slump into a new order

blocks.note: a stud is a womaniser, as Casanova was
taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An apprentice lothario online finds himself unable to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: Casanova, the famous Venetian seducer, stands for any ladies' man, and 'floppy' does double duty in the surface's joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in training is learning, and a learner at a college or school is a pupil of that kind.

clue.text: Trump payee, far from calm

blocks.note: first meaning: the first name of the adult-film actress paid hush money on Trump's behalf
second meaning: turbulent, tempestuous weather or temper

explanation.surface: Someone paid by Trump turns out to be anything but placid.
explanation.walkthrough: The payee is Stormy Daniels, the actress whose hush-money payment led to Trump's criminal case.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent weather with wind and rain is the opposite of still, and the name belongs to Stormy Daniels.
